text:
[RLOW.4.6.2.1] State: `(rule_name, activation_key) → last_fire_ns`. The
activation key is the sequence of values [LCDB.3.3.3] composes, and **two keys
are the same key only if they have the same length and, position by position,
values of the same representation that are equal.** `1`, `"1"` and `true` are
three keys, not one. The representation is the value's tag, not its declared
type ([LNUL.4.9]), so a `Time` and an `Int` holding the same count are one key.

Equality within a representation is the language's `==` for a scalar — `0.0`
and `-0.0` are one key — deep structural equality for `Json` ([LFAC.2.5.1]),
and `null` equals only `null`. The comparison is **exact and whole**: nothing is
rounded, truncated or compared by prefix, and a key has no length limit of its
own. How a runtime stores a key is its own, provided the storage preserves this
identity.

idris.name: Rlow_4_6_2_1__key
idris.note: The key: the components in [LCDB.3.3.3]'s order, as a list of canonical parts.

idris.name: Rlow_4_6_2_1__part
idris.note: One component: a value under its representation's tag ([LNUL.4.9]), in the canonical form that representation compares by -- a Float by its bits with the two zeros one pattern, a Json by its canonical text, a String or Bytes by its bytes, null by itself -- so that 'equal under the representation' is structural equality of the part. Partial because the canonical forms are taken as given, not derived from the representations' equalities; and a value no representation carries (libds's RK_UNBOUND, the Mercury runtime's kp_unexpanded for a broken artefact) has no constructor, since the clause composes a key from values.

idris.name: Rlow_4_6_2_1__same
idris.note: THE IDENTITY, as the clause words it: the same length, and position by position the same canonical part.

idris.name: Rlow_4_6_2_1__word
idris.note: libds's word codec -- how `rk_feed_u64` writes a 64-bit count into a stored key and how a reader takes it back -- as a parameter: two functions, taken at the contract `Rlow_4_6_2_1__word_ok` states rather than modelled byte by byte. The real codec, eight little-endian bytes, runs in Main.idr.

idris.name: Rlow_4_6_2_1__word_ok
idris.note: The codec's contract: a word written in front of anything reads back as that word and leaves the rest. What eight little-endian bytes have for every value a uint64 holds, and the one hypothesis the storage theorems take.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__bool_of
idris.note: A Bool's word read back: libds writes 1 or 0.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__bytes_rt
idris.note: A length-prefixed component written reads back whole and leaves what followed it, for every byte string and every tail: no byte a component holds can end it early, and none is cut.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__bytes_then
idris.note: A length-prefixed component read back: the word says how many bytes are the component's.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__cons_of
idris.note: A component read in front of the components read after it.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__decode
idris.note: The key read back from libds's frame: the count, then that many components, and nothing left over. libds has no reader -- it compares keys in place -- and the reader is written because one that inverts the writer is what makes the writer injective.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__decode_encode
idris.note: THE KEY WRITTEN READS BACK: the reader inverts libds's frame on every key, under every codec with the contract.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__drop_app
idris.note: Dropping a list's own length from in front of a tail leaves the tail. A list lemma of this standalone module's own.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__encode
idris.note: THE KEY AS libds STORES IT (`rk_walk`, rete/adapters.c): the component count, then per component a tag byte and a fixed-width word or a length word and the bytes. 'How a runtime stores a key is its own, provided the storage preserves this identity': this is libds's storage, and `rlow_4_6_2_1__encode_injective` is that it preserves the identity.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__encode_injective
idris.note: libds's STORAGE PRESERVES THE IDENTITY: two keys stored as one byte string are one key, for every pair of keys and every codec with the contract. The count, the tag bytes and the length words make the frame prefix-free, so a component may hold any byte and any length.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__equal_is_same
idris.note: A key is the same key as itself, so the relation is exactly equality.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__field_of
idris.note: One component read back: the tag byte decides the shape, the word the value or the length.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__field_rt
idris.note: A component written reads back and leaves exactly what followed it, for every component of every representation and every tail.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__field_to
idris.note: One component's bytes, `rk_walk`'s arm for its kind: a tag byte for the representation, then a word for a scalar, or a word giving the length and then the bytes for a String, Bytes or Json; null its tag alone; a Ratio two words.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__fields_of
idris.note: So many components read back, in order.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__fields_rt
idris.note: The components written read back, as many as were written, and leave exactly what followed them.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__fields_to
idris.note: The components' bytes in the key's order.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__int_is_not_the_bool
idris.note: The integer 1 and the boolean true are two keys: two representations. By the constructors.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__int_is_not_the_string
idris.note: '`1`, `"1"` and `true` are three keys, not one': the integer 1 and the string "1" (its one byte, 0x31) are two keys. By the constructors.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__just_inj
idris.note: `Just` is injective; the base has no `Injective Just` and this module imports nothing of the lane.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__negative_zero_is_zero
idris.note: The negative zero's pattern keys as the zero, for every pattern that stands for it.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__of_float
idris.note: A Float keys by the bits of its double, the negative zero's pattern read as the positive zero's: '`0.0` and `-0.0` are one key'. The pattern of -0.0 is a parameter so the rule is stated without a 64-bit literal; both runtimes make the normalisation as they key.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__of_time
idris.note: A Time keys as its count, an Int: 'the representation is the value's tag, not its declared type'. There is no constructor for a Time; a Date or a Duration takes the same function.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__ratio_of
idris.note: A Ratio's second word read back after its first.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__ratio_rt
idris.note: A Ratio's second word reads back after its first.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__same_b
idris.note: The key compared, exact and whole: the same length, then component by component. The executable form of the identity, run in Main.idr; not proved equal to `Rlow_4_6_2_1__same`.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__same_is_equality
idris.note: THE IDENTITY IS EQUALITY OF THE KEY: two keys the clause calls the same are one list of canonical parts -- what a `map` keyed on the Mercury runtime's `rate_key` compares (ds.rate.m), so that storage preserves the identity by construction.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__same_part_b
idris.note: One component compared: the same representation and an equal value under it; two representations are two components whatever the values.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__string_is_not_the_bool
idris.note: The string "1" and the boolean true are two keys: the third pair of the clause's example.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__take_app
idris.note: Taking a list's own length from in front of a tail gives the list. A list lemma of this standalone module's own.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__time_keys_as_int
idris.note: 'A `Time` and an `Int` holding the same count are one key', for every count. A transcription of `rlow_4_6_2_1__of_time`, `Refl`.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__whole_of
idris.note: The components read back are the key when nothing is left over.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__word_rt
idris.note: A scalar component written reads back and leaves what followed it, for every word and every tail.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__word_then
idris.note: A scalar component read back: one word, under the constructor its tag named.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__zero_is_zero
idris.note: The zero keys as itself whatever pattern stands for the negative one: the normalisation touches nothing else.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__zeros_one_key
idris.note: '`0.0` and `-0.0` are one key', for every pattern of the negative zero.

idris.name: Iret_10_4__trackers
idris.note: State `(rule_name, activation_key) -> last_fire_ns`, keyed on the rule's ordinal and the activation key's CODE: the value code of the key's tuple, whose equality is the clause's identity -- the same length and, per position, the same representation tag and an equal value under it -- by the code's construction, run and not proved (Main.idr, THE VALUE CODE). Partial for that: the identity is the code's, not derived from the representations.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__same_key
idris.note: Two tracker keys are one key when the rule and the key code are equal: the clause's identity through the value code, whose injectivity is run and not proved.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__same_key_is_equality
idris.note: TWO KEYS THE TABLE CALLS THE SAME ARE ONE PAIR: the identity is equality of the rule and the code, over every pair of keys.

idris.name: rlow_4_6_2_1__same_key_refl
idris.note: A key is the same key as itself.
